result.topic_en: Problem 3 asks for a curve whose ordinates take given values at abscissas in arithmetic progression. The solution builds an interpolation series whose coefficients are expressed through a Beta-type integral Δ.
result.transcription:
-) 184 (-
Problema 3.
§. 30. Inuenire eiusmodi aequationem pro linea curua inter binas variabiles, abscissam $x$ et applicatam $y$, vt abscissis, in arithmetica progressione sumtis, datae conueniant applicatae, scilicet:
Si fit $x = n\theta,\ (n+1)\theta,\ (n+2)\theta,\ (n+3)\theta,\ (n+4)\theta,$ etc.
vt fiat $y = p,\quad q,\quad r,\quad s,\quad t,$ etc.
Solutio.
Ponamus in genere $x=\theta\omega$, atque ex solutione generali §. 10. data consequimur hanc aequationem:
$\frac{y}{\omega} = \frac{p}{n}\cdot\frac{(n+1-\omega)(n+1+\omega)}{1(2n+1)}\cdot\frac{(n+2-\omega)(n+2+\omega)}{2(2n+2)}\cdot\frac{(n+3-\omega)(n+3+\omega)}{3(2n+3)}$ etc.
$-\frac{q}{n+1}\cdot\frac{(n-\omega)(n+\omega)}{1(2n+1)}\cdot\frac{(n+2-\omega)(n+2+\omega)}{1(2n+3)}\cdot\frac{(n+3-\omega)(n+3+\omega)}{2(2n+4)}$ etc. [?]
$+\frac{r}{n+2}\cdot\frac{(n-\omega)(n+\omega)}{2(2n+2)}\cdot\frac{(n+1-\omega)(n+1+\omega)}{1(2n+3)}\cdot\frac{(n+3-\omega)(n+3+\omega)}{1(2n+5)}$ etc. [?]
etc.
quam aequationem breuitatis gratia ita repraesentemus:
$\frac{y}{\omega} = \mathfrak{A}\cdot\frac{p}{n} - \mathfrak{B}\cdot\frac{q}{n+1} + \mathfrak{C}\cdot\frac{r}{n+2} - \mathfrak{D}\cdot\frac{s}{n+3} +$ etc.
ac primo quidem pro valore ipsius $\mathfrak{A}$ eliciendo ex forma generali §. 17 allata pro hoc casu habebimus
$a = n+1-\omega;\ b = 1,\ c = n+1+\omega$ et $d = 1$,
vnde per formulas integrales, a termino $z=0$ ad $z=1$ extendendas, colligimus
$\mathfrak{A} = \frac{\int dz(1-z)^{n-\omega-1}}{\int z^{n-\omega}dz(1-z)^{n-\omega-1}} = \frac{1}{(n-\omega)\int z^{n-\omega}dz(1-z)^{n-\omega-1}}$,
seu
$\mathfrak{A} = \frac{2}{(n-\omega)\int z^{n-\omega-1}dz(1-z)^{n-\omega-1}}$,
qua

-) 185 (-
qua integratione concessa reliqua facile expediuntur. Erit enim vt supra §. 17
$\frac{\mathfrak{B}}{\mathfrak{A}} = \frac{(n-\omega)(n+\omega)}{(n+1-\omega)(n+1+\omega)}\cdot(2+2n) = \frac{2(n+1)(n-\omega)(n+\omega)}{(n+1-\omega)(n+1+\omega)}$,
$\frac{\mathfrak{C}}{\mathfrak{B}} = \frac{(n+1-\omega)(n+1+\omega)}{(n+2-\omega)(n+2+\omega)}\cdot\frac{(1+2n)(2+2n)}{2(1+n)}$ [?],
$\frac{\mathfrak{D}}{\mathfrak{C}} = \frac{(n+2-\omega)(n+2+\omega)}{(n+3-\omega)(n+3+\omega)}\cdot\frac{(2+2n)(3+2n)}{3(n+2)}$ [?],
$\frac{\mathfrak{E}}{\mathfrak{D}} = \frac{(n+3-\omega)(n+3+\omega)}{(n+4-\omega)(n+4+\omega)}\cdot\frac{(3+2n)(4+2n)}{4(n+3)}$ [?],
etc.
Statuamus igitur formulam integralem:
$\int z^{n-\omega-1}dz(1-z)^{n-\omega-1} = \Delta$,
vt fit $\mathfrak{A} = \frac{2}{(n-\omega)\Delta}$, et reliqui coefficientes ita per $\mathfrak{A}$ definientur:
$\mathfrak{B} = \frac{2(n+1)}{1}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(n+1)^2-\omega\omega}\mathfrak{A}$
$\mathfrak{C} = \frac{2(n+1)(2n+1)}{1\cdot 2}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(n+2)^2-\omega\omega}\mathfrak{A}$
$\mathfrak{D} = \frac{2(n+2)(2n+1)(2n+3)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(n+3)^2-\omega\omega}\mathfrak{A}$ [?]
$\mathfrak{E} = \frac{2(n+4)(2n+1)(2n+2)(2n+3)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot 4}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{(n+4)^2-\omega\omega}\mathfrak{A}$ [?]
etc.
Quamobrem aequatio quaesita inter $y$ et $x=\theta\omega$, ita erit comparata:
$\frac{n\Delta y}{2(n+\omega)\omega} = \frac{p}{nn-\omega\omega} - \frac{2n}{1}\cdot\frac{q}{(n+1)^2-\omega\omega} + \frac{2n(2n+1)}{1\cdot 2}\cdot\frac{r}{(n+2)^2-\omega\omega} - \frac{2n(2n+1)(2n+2)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3}\cdot\frac{s}{(n+3)^2-\omega\omega} +$ etc.
vnde pro quouis valore ipsius $x=\theta\omega$ conueniens ipsius $y$ valor definitur; idque per applicatas $p, q, r$, etc. quae abscissis $n\theta$, $(n+1)\theta$, $(n+2)\theta$, etc. conuenientes assumuntur. Vbi quidem notari oportet, si $\omega$ capiatur aequalis cuipiam termino progressionis $n$, $n+1$, $n+2$, etc. tum deno-
Euleri Opusc. Anal. Tom. I. Aa

items.quote: Inuenire eiusmodi aequationem pro linea curua inter binas variabiles, abscissam $x$ et applicatam $y$, vt abscissis, in arithmetica progressione sumtis, datae conueniant applicatae
items.english: To find an equation for a curved line between two variables, abscissa x and ordinate y, such that given ordinates correspond to abscissas taken in arithmetic progression.
